meta.title: Who really said "Fashion is always a reflection of the times, but it is forgotten if it is foolish"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Coco Chanel really wrote it — in French. Traced to her "Maximes et Sentences" in Vogue Paris, September 1938, page 56. The English is a later rendering.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'Fashion is always a reflection of the times, but it is forgotten if it is foolish'?
meta.ogDescription: Genuine, but written in French: Chanel published it in "Maximes et Sentences," Vogue Paris, September 1938, p. 56. The English is one of several renderings.

answer.label: Written by
answer.authorDates: 1883–1971 · French couturière, founder of the House of Chanel
answer.sourceLine: Chanel published this among thirty-one aphorisms headed “Maximes et Sentences” in the September 1938 issue of Vogue (Paris), page 56. The French reads “La mode est toujours un reflet de l’époque, mais on l’oublie si elle est bête” — the English you see here is one of several defensible renderings, and no named translator owns this particular wording.

source.heading: The source

docMeta.dd: Written in French; the circulating English is a modern rendering with no identified translator

source.excerpt:
“La mode est toujours un reflet de l’époque, mais on l’oublie si elle est bête.”

“Fashion is always a reflection of the times, but it is forgotten if it is foolish.”
trail: September 1938 — Vogue (Paris) runs a two-page spread of maxims by Chanel. The issue’s contents list, in the BnF’s digitised 1938 volume, reads “MAXIMES ET SENTENCES, par Gabrielle Chanel 56” — and the full-text index returns the sentence itself on the maxims page (Gallica, BnF ↗).
The magazine. The BnF’s bibliographic record confirms Vogue (Paris) was published by Condé Nast from 1920 and that the digitised run sits on Gallica (Catalogue général, BnF ↗).

2009 — Karen Karbo’s The Gospel According to Coco Chanel quotes the line in English as “fashion is always a reflection of its own time, but we forget this when it is stupid” — a different rendering of the same French (Quote Investigator, citing Karbo p. 223 ↗).
2021 — Quote Investigator publishes the trace, naming the September 1938 Vogue as the origin and noting the saying admits several English translations (quoteinvestigator.com ↗).
source.excerptNote: One item in a two-page spread of aphorisms Chanel published under her own name. Gallica’s full-text index of the 1938 Vogue volume returns this sentence on the maxims page, immediately followed by the next maxim, which begins “Se déguiser est charmant…”

author.name: Coco Chanel
author.heading: Who was Coco Chanel?
author.metaLine: 1883–1971 · French couturière and founder of the House of Chanel
author.bio: Gabrielle Bonheur Chanel, called Coco, rose from a charity orphanage to become the couturière who made casual, unfussy elegance the feminine standard after the First World War — jersey, costume pearls, and the No. 5 scent. She registered as a couturière by 1919 and built her house at 31 rue Cambon in Paris, closing it at the outbreak of war in 1939 and reopening in 1954. She also wrote: aphorisms published under her name in magazines, of which this is one, though her biographers suspect the poet Pierre Reverdy had a hand in sharpening them.

misattribution.heading: What usually goes wrong
misattribution.intro: The attribution here holds up unusually well for a Chanel line. What wobbles is the English, and — more interestingly — who actually polished the French.

items.why: Chanel wrote “…mais on l’oublie si elle est bête.” Quote Investigator offers “but we forget it if it is stupid”; Karen Karbo’s 2009 book has “but we forget this when it is stupid.” The familiar “but it is forgotten if it is foolish” is a smoother third rendering, and no published translator is identified behind it (Quote Investigator ↗).

BrainyQuote’s Chanel page does not carry this sentence at all. What it circulates is a shorter, separate line — “Fashion is always of the time in which you live” — offered with no source, date or publication (BrainyQuote ↗).

Chanel’s biographer Edmonde Charles-Roux argued that the polished maxims published under Chanel’s name in periodicals were shaped with the poet Pierre Reverdy — who corrected the aphorisms she wrote about her trade and added others of his own on wider subjects. It is a scholarly conjecture, not a documented fact about this particular sentence (Wikipedia, citing Charles-Roux, Chanel and Her World, 1981, p. 328 ↗).
The line travels almost everywhere as a bare English epigram with no publication attached. English Wikiquote’s Chanel page does not list it in its sourced section at all (Wikiquote ↗).

misattribution.truthLine: The thought and the sentence are genuinely Chanel’s, printed under her name in Vogue Paris in September 1938 — it is only the English clothing that came later (Quote Investigator ↗).

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Chanel was fifty-five when the maxims ran — born 19 August 1883, so the September 1938 issue caught her a few weeks past that birthday. It was not a comfortable moment. Elsa Schiaparelli’s surrealist wit was drawing the acclaim, and Chanel’s excursion into Hollywood costume had gone badly. A spread of aphorisms in Vogue reads, in that light, less like a victory lap than a designer restating her creed while the spotlight moved.

Within a year the creed had to wait: Chanel closed the couture house at the outbreak of war in 1939 and did not reopen it until 1954. The sentence she published in 1938 turned out to describe her own career — a style that reflected its era, went quiet, and was not forgotten.
detailsBody: The French turns on two flexible words. “On l’oublie” is an impersonal construction that goes into English either actively (“we forget it”) or passively (“it is forgotten”) with equal warrant. And “bête” covers a range English splits up — silly, stupid, foolish, daft — with “foolish” the most literary of the options.
That is why three published renderings can all be faithful and none of them canonical. The version that spread is the most quotable one, which is usually how these things get settled.
context.pull: The line is Chanel’s. The English is somebody else’s.

sourcesVerified.claim: Quote Investigator traces the quote to Gabrielle Chanel's "Maximes et Sentences" in the September 1938 Vogue (Paris), quote page 56, gives the French original "La mode est toujours un reflet de l'époque, mais on l'oublie si elle est bête," offers the translation "Fashion is always a reflection of the times, but we forget it if it is stupid," and cites Karen Karbo's 2009 The Gospel According to Coco Chanel, p. 223, for "fashion is always a reflection of its own time, but we forget this when it is stupid."

BnF Gallica's full-text search inside the 1938 Vogue (Paris) volume (ark bpt6k936228j) returns the exact phrase "La mode est toujours un reflet de l'époque, mais on l'oublie si elle est [bête]" on the maxims page, and the contents-page entry "MAXIMES ET SENTENCES, par Gabrielle Chanel 56" — independently confirming Quote Investigator's page-56 citation.

BnF's record for ark bpt6k936228j identifies it as Vogue, 1938, published by Condé Nast (Paris), shelfmark FOL-V-5554 (BIS), and labels its rights "domaine public" / "public domain" — a determination under French law only.

This Gallica viewer URL is the BnF's digitised 1938 volume of Vogue (Paris) containing Chanel's "Maximes et Sentences." Identity of the ark was confirmed by fetching BnF's own OAI record and full-text ContentSearch service for the same ark; the viewer page itself sits behind a bot check.
The BnF catalogue record for Vogue (Paris) confirms publication by Condé Nast, Paris, 1920–2021, and gives the Gallica reproduction URL for the digitised run.

Wikipedia gives Chanel's dates as 19 August 1883 – 10 January 1971, describes her as a French fashion designer and businesswoman, records that she closed the couture house in 1939 and reopened in 1954, and states it is postulated that the maxims attributed to Chanel and published in periodicals were crafted under the mentorship of Pierre Reverdy — citing Edmonde Charles-Roux, Chanel and Her World (Weidenfeld and Nicolson, 1981), p. 328, that Reverdy corrected the aphorisms Chanel wrote about her métier and added further thoughts of his own.
English Wikiquote's Coco Chanel page does not contain "Fashion is always a reflection of the time(s)" or the French original, and has no Misattributed or Disputed section.

BrainyQuote's Coco Chanel page does not carry this sentence; the nearest fashion line it lists is "Fashion is always of the time in which you live," and the page gives no source citation for any of its Chanel quotes.

The Internet Archive holds a scan of Karen Karbo's The Gospel According to Coco Chanel: Life Lessons from the World's Most Elegant Woman (2009) under identifier gospelaccordingt0000karb — the book Quote Investigator cites for an alternate English rendering.
